title: Naturality of open-support comparison in the compactifications
statement: Use E(cf,cp) from [def-asd-open-support-compactification-model]. Let a ≫ f = p ≫ j be a cartesian square, with a,j open immersions and f,p quasi-compact, and let cf,df be compactifications of f and cp,dp compactifications of p. Let I(c,d) be the canonical common-refinement comparison of unbounded compact support. Then (I(cp,dp).hom ▷ Dj!) ≫ E(df,dp).hom = E(cf,cp).hom ≫ (Da! ◁ I(cf,df).hom). This is a two-dimensional naturality square involving no external base-change square.

proof.text: Use etaleGraphComparisonBaseChange to prove that changing the source compactification before a specified graph map agrees with that graph map. Normalize graph comparisons to common-refinement comparisons. Use the single-refinement graph normalization to identify a graph map along a cartesian refinement with its specified rho. Deduce G(b,d);rho(r)=G(b,c). These are proved Lean helper theorems, with no new holes.

Factor the supplied support comparison as G(b,cU) whiskered by Dj!, followed by the explicit graph-free P(c). Apply the one-refinement exchange equation, then the graph/refinement composition identity, to prove E(d,b);Da!rho(r)=E(c,b). The graph source-change law also proves I(b,d)Dj!;E(c,d)=E(c,b).

Take the actual common refinement inf(cf,df) and its two cartesian projections. Apply the preceding refinement identities and source-change law. Expand I(cf,df) as rho(infFst);rho(infSnd)^(-1). Solve the second refinement identity by postcomposition with its inverse, and substitute. Reassociate, use source-change naturality, and then the first refinement identity. Both sides become E(inf,cp) followed by the inverse of Da!rho(infSnd), proving the original equation.

proof_origin.place: Coherence (i): existing graph normalization and cocycle theorem, the single-cartesian-refinement exchange calculation, then common-refinement cancellation.

theorem openSupportCompactificationIso_naturality
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X Y U V : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [QuasiCompact f]
    {j : U ⟶ Y} [IsOpenImmersion j] {a : V ⟶ X} [IsOpenImmersion a]
    {p : V ⟶ U} [QuasiCompact p] (sq : IsPullback a p f j)
    (cf df : Compactification f) (cp dp : Compactification p) :
    Functor.whiskerRight (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso Λ cp dp).hom
        D((j)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ≫
      (openSupportCompactificationIso Λ sq df dp).hom =
    (openSupportCompactificationIso Λ sq cf cp).hom ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft D((a)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso Λ cf df).hom
